analysis: The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is a documentation-only addition at head lines 2513-2520. It describes decode-kernel fusion: fused q/k/v and gate+up matmuls, routed gate/up banks fused at load, compiled router steps, and a single MoE combine/shared-expert/residual kernel. It claims byte-identical outputs and a drop from about 2,000 to about 1,200 GPU primitives per token. The supplied units are unchanged base context (lines 802-1610), and the patch touches no code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-handling paths. I checked the added text against the threat model. T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier, TTL, HMAC lookup tags) and the other cache and attestation entries are not affected by it. T-007 (provider output manipulation) and TB-007 (inference engine) are not weakened, because the text asserts output equivalence and does not alter any trust claim. Neither the patch nor the supplied context shows the corresponding source change, so the byte-identical claim and the checkpoint validation in split form are unverified here. If the source implements fused load-time weight banks, a later pass should confirm that weight-hash and template validation (T-012, T-027) still run on the split form. That is an integration question, not a finding against this documentation diff. I identified no security regression and no need to update the threat model from this change.
